title: I took your feedback and kept working on Portal Beasts — new worlds, redesigned beasts, and a new gameplay trailer
author: PortalBeasts
selftext:
Hey everyone!

A while ago, I shared Portal Beasts here, my solo-developed monster-catching action RPG. Some of you tried the demo, asked about the development process, or pointed out things that needed work. I wanted to come back with an update and show where the game is now.

For anyone seeing it for the first time: you directly control your beasts in real-time battles, moving, aiming attacks, and dodging or shielding.

One comment on my previous post pointed out that trees had shadows while the characters and beasts didn’t. That was a fair point, and it led to quite a bit of work on shadows, sprite positioning, and making everything feel like it belongs in the same game.

Here’s what else I’ve been working on:

* **A more consistent color palette.** I reworked environment colors and outlines, then went back over assets where the changes had lost detail or made materials look wrong.
* **New worlds.** Volcanic forests, tropical islands, and a swamp with shallow water you can wade through.
* **New and redesigned beasts**, including new evolutions and more complete directional animations.
* **Combat improvements.** Clearer hit effects, adjustments to hit detection and movement speed, and more work on how enemies choose their attacks and use defensive abilities.
* **Beasts helping outside combat.** Water beasts can pull your raft between islands.
* **UI and controls.** A revised interface, remappable controls, and an optional quick-cast mode.

I’ve put together a new 90-second gameplay trailer showing the current version. It includes areas being developed for the full game; the free demo covers the town, Mosswood, and Hollowwood, up to your first Portal Ranger exam.

I’m still using Godot, with AI-assisted coding and art tools alongside Aseprite and purchased assets. Getting the results to work together has meant a lot of testing and reworking things.

I’d love to hear how this compares with the earlier version. Does the art feel more consistent now, and can you clearly follow what’s happening during combat?

[**Play the free demo on Steam**](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4545580/Portal_Beasts_Demo/)

Thanks for taking another look!  
Lasse

comments.author: Askanio234
comments.body: Wow this is nice, what is your workflow for the animations? They look super smooth.

replies.author: PortalBeasts
replies.body: Pixellab, character editor. Lets Chatgpt, Gemini etc, to make a prompt for the character. Then makes states in the character editor, mid walk, mid jump, etc. pixellab have a ai to enhance a prompt if needed

comments.author: Foreign-Quote-53
comments.body:
To me, the characters and Ui look very generic. In general the style is generic. And still doesn’t look consistent to me. Are all pixels the same density? It’s kind of hard to tell, they probably are but the vast difference in detail from object to object makes me question it. I think the perspective on objects don’t look consistent and you can see a lot of assets repeating, like trees and floor tiles.

I think it’s also jarring to watch the little guys fight and clearly hit the “trainers” but they donMt react at all. They should be off to the side, cheering, reacting to attacks and hits and what not.

I’ve been pretty negative, but from the trailer looks like you have a good start and I could see people being interested in the project.

replies.author: PortalBeasts
replies.body:
I had decided to turn off damage for the player/trainer, because the trainer died and ended the battle. I don't know how else to do it to make it work better, since the trainer can still die if he runs out of beasts.

I also think that sometimes being generic is a good thing, so there isn't too much going on. Could you give some examples of what you mean by inconsistent, so I can possibly work on it for next time?

replies.author: Foreign-Quote-53
replies.body:
Well I think the trainers not dying it probably a good thing, but they probably shouldn’t just stand there as attacks phase through them

For instance, like the trees are very detailed, but then the grass is just like a flat green. It stands out most in like that night area to me

replies.author: PortalBeasts
replies.body: And yes, it's an ambitious project, but I've been working on it for a long time, and I hope to finish it one day.

comments.author: No_Bass_8636
comments.body:
I think a lot of the style clashes with each other. Some of the monsters have selective outlining, most are solid black outlining including the humans. World assets don't have consistent outlining. 

Morphy, Bludbun, and Dogcano look like they're all from different games. I think you need to take a look at other pixel art creature collector rosters and see how they look against each other. For example, gen 3 sprites of Igglybuff and Wailord. Wailord is magnitudes bigger, but due to the same canvas size and good work with perspective you can tell that they exist in the same world and their scales are clear, even if they are next to each other in battle. 

I can see you've improved the UI, but it's still not very good. Has such little art to it and I think the layout is still such a basic boilerplate AI style.
